title: PT1 — Chemical Reactions Around Me: Photo Essay & Equation Journal
summary: Document real chemical reactions in your daily life with photos, then write balanced chemical equations and brief explanations for each one.
instructions:
Your task is to create a photo essay + equation journal that captures at least 5 real chemical reactions happening around you. You will:

  1. Photograph 5 different chemical reactions you observe in daily life. Examples:
    • Cooking — caramelizing sugar, toasting bread (Maillard reaction), browning meat
    • Cleaning — vinegar on baking soda, bleach on stains
    • Burning — LPG stove flame, candle, matchstick, barbecue
    • Rusting — old gate, bike chain, exposed iron
    • Food preservation — sliced apple turning brown, milk souring
    • Biological — cut healing, leaf decaying, fermentation in bread dough
  2. For each photo, identify the type of reaction (decomposition, combustion, acid on carbonate, acid on metal, oxidation, photosynthesis, respiration, etc.).
  3. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
  4. Write a 3–4 sentence explanation of what's happening chemically and why it matters.
  5. Add a short reflection at the end (1 paragraph) about how this task changed the way you see chemistry around you.

Format: PDF, DOCX, or PowerPoint (5+ slides). Submit as a file, or paste a share link in the reflection.
requirements: At least 5 different chemical reactions documented with photos
Reaction type clearly identified for each photo
Balanced chemical equation for each reaction
Personal reflection paragraph at the end
Proper citation if any external sources used

rubric.criterion: Number and variety of reactions captured (5+)
Quality of photos and overall presentation
